mutants.expected_detection: Compiling with -DAEAD_TEST_COUNTER_START=0xFFFFFFFD and issuing repeated calls shows that after the counter reaches 0xFFFFFFFF and one more call is made, the function silently wraps the counter back to 0 and returns 0, reproducing the exact nonce/ciphertext pattern that a fresh run at counter 0 would produce (nonce reuse), instead of returning a nonzero error code and halting further encryption.

Pre-fill ciphertext_out and tag_out with sentinel bytes, drive the counter to exhaustion via AEAD_TEST_COUNTER_START near 0xFFFFFFFF, and observe that on the exhausting call (which returns -1) the tag_out buffer no longer contains the untouched sentinel bytes because the mutant still computes and writes the tag before returning the error code.

Compiling with -DAEAD_TEST_COUNTER_START=0xFFFFFFFD and calling aead_encrypt_call repeatedly will show that at counter==0xFFFFFFFF the exhaustion check `counter == 0xFFFFFFFFu && have_used_max` is never true on the very first visit to max (have_used_max starts false), so encryption proceeds and increments the counter, but because the increment branch was swapped to execute the increment unconditionally (using counter++ instead of the guarded branch), the counter silently wraps to 0 on the call after max is used, causing the next call to reuse counter value 0's nonce identically to the very first call -- violating the requirement that the exhaustion check occur before any wraparound side effects and that wraparound never silently occur.

Calling aead_encrypt_call repeatedly with the same key/plaintext should yield a different ciphertext/tag each time (since the nonce block changes with the counter). This mutant hardcodes the nonce-block counter bytes to a fixed constant (0) instead of using the actual counter_value parameter, so build_nonce_block always builds the same nonce regardless of the internal counter. FR1's check that repeated calls with a fixed key/plaintext produce different ciphertext/tag pairs on each call will fail because every call produces byte-identical ciphertext and tag output despite the counter incrementing internally.

Harness calls aead_encrypt_call with plaintext_len == 16 (or any value <16 not a multiple of 16 boundary case) while counter has capacity, and checks that exactly 16 bytes of tag are written and exactly plaintext_len bytes of ciphertext are written; this mutant truncates the tag write to 15 bytes, so a byte-exact comparison of tag_out against the reference tag (or a check that byte 15 was actually written/changed from a sentinel) will fail, violating FR2's requirement that exactly 16 bytes be written to tag_out on every successful call.

g++ compilation of the submission against the test harness and AES primitive stub fails with a hard error (undeclared identifier 'std::optional' / missing header, or use of a C++17-only construct without the required include), so synthesis_pass_rate drops to 0 for this submission even though the logic would otherwise be correct. This violates FR3's requirement that the file must compile cleanly as a standalone translation unit with g++ (C++11 or later) with no external dependencies beyond the standard library and the AES primitive stub.

Calling aead_encrypt_call with plaintext_len == 0 (while counter has capacity) must return 0 and write exactly 16 bytes to tag_out with zero bytes written to ciphertext_out. This mutant negates the loop guard so the encryption while-loop body executes even when plaintext_len == 0, causing an out-of-contract write to ciphertext_out (writing at least one keystream byte) and mismatched behavior versus reference on the zero-length-plaintext test vector required by FR4.
